discussion_comments.comment_body: `prepareHandoffRepository` isn't in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS` in #15205, so it won't be reachable through the Hub client. It's also called in both prepare and run (via `resolveCloudModel`), along with `loadCloudModels` and 8 `assertHandoffAccount` calls. Resolving once and carrying a scope token in the snapshot would remove most of the repeated checks.

The missing Hub operation is fixed: `prepareHandoffRepository` is registered in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS`, validated by the Hub service, and exposed by `CloudHubClient`. The preparation snapshot also captures a `CloudHubScope`, which subsequent operations carry so they cannot silently switch accounts. Socket coverage exercises repository preparation, and account-scope tests cover changes during recovery. This addresses the RPC compatibility issue; it does not remove the repeated model/repository checks.

Suggestion: make the visibility filter unconditional and drop `mcpApps` from `CreateMcpToolsOptions`.

The spec says the host MUST NOT list tools whose visibility doesn't include `"model"`, with no exception for hosts that haven't advertised the apps extension. A tool tagged `visibility: ["app"]` is never meant for the model, so hiding it when apps are off is still the right behavior (there's no app around to call it either).

That leaves the client factory flag as the single switch for MCP Apps, and removes the "the two must be set together" caveat from DOC.md. Conformant servers only send `_meta.ui` tools after the client advertises the capability anyway, so the factory flag is the real gate.

Not blocking, approving as is. It's just cheaper to collapse this now than after the option is in the published `@cline/core` surface. Feel free to make the change and I can re-review.

The VS Code translator renders `displayPrompt`, so an answer such as `Use @/spec.txt` remains exactly that in the chat bubble and edit surface instead of exposing the resolved file content.

The regression now exercises a resolved prompt alongside the original display text and verifies that attachments remain attached to the displayed user feedback. 🟢 **bug** (low)

The value sent in the `X-Task-ID` request header changed from the task ID to the ulid while the header name (and therefore the contract the Cline backend sees) stayed the same. If the backend treats this header as a task identifier (attribution, rate limiting, server-side joins), the meaning of the header silently changed; for tasks that have no ulid the header is also now empty where it previously always carried a value. This is probably intended as part of "ulid everywhere", but the header name no longer describes its content.

**建议**: Confirm with the backend owner which identifier this header is expected to carry, then either keep sending the task ID or rename the header (e.g. `X-Task-ULID`) so the contract stays unambiguous. If both ids are needed, send them as separate headers.

**证据**: `"X-Task-ID": this.options.ulid || "",`
